    MA4704 · AEROELASTICITY

    Static Aeroelasticity

    #Rigid Wing Divergence

    Wing divergence:

    • Effects of aerodynamic loads on the elastic deformation of a structure
    • Divergence — the potential for static instability to result in structural failure
    • Occurs when wing deforms under aerodynamic loads in such a way that increases
      the applied load, which will then deflect the wing further, eventually leading to failure
    • Interaction of aerodynamic loads with the structure creates a loss of effective stiffness

    Consider a rigid, spanwise-uniform wing mounted to the side walls of a wind tunnel
    such that the wing is allowed to pitch about its support axis. The support is flexible
    in torsion and restricts the pitch rotation of the wing similar to a torsional spring.

    If the support was rigid, initial angle of attack of the wing will be purely αr​.
    As the elastic support is non-rigid, there is an additional angle of attack θ.

    Wing angle of attack is then,

    α=αr​+θ

    Assuming incompressible flow,

    L=21​ρU2SCL​=qSCLα​​α

    Mac​=21​ρU2SCM​c=qSCMac​​c

    As this is a static analysis, moments about the elastic axis ∑M=0.

    0=Mac​+(Lcosα)e−kθ

    0=qSCMac​​c+(qSCLα​​α)(cosα)e−kθ

    0=qSCMac​​c+qSCLα​​(αr​+θ)e−kθ

    💡

    θ=k−qSCLα​​eqSCMac​​c+qSCLα​​αr​e​

    where e is the distance between elastic axis and aerodynamic center

    #Divergence Dynamic Pressure qD​ & Airspeed UD​

    From the above equation, when e is positive:

    • Elastic axis is located behind the aerodynamic center
    • Specific k and e values exists such that denominator equals zero
    • Denominator equals zero → θ becomes infinity → divergence occurs

    Dynamic pressure and airspeed at which divergence occurs,

    💡

    qD​=SCLα​​ek​

    💡

    UD​=ρSCLα​​e2k​​

    When e≤0, elastic axis is located at or forward of aerodynamic center,
    Denominator     =0 and the occurrence of divergence is impossible.
    Rigid support     k=∞, divergence will not occur since qD​=∞.

    #Example 1

    Distance between ac and elastic axis,

    e=2c​−4c​=4c​=0.05 m

    Total torsional stiffness of the beams,

    k=2(LGIP​​)=2[LG(πd4/32)​]

    k=2[0.4(9×1010)π(0.0154/32)​]

    k=2236.5 Nm

    Divergence dynamic pressure,

    qD​=SCLα​​ek​=(bc)CLα​​ek​

    qD​=(1.2×0.2)(5.2)(0.05)2236.5​

    qD​=35840.1 N/m2

    Divergence airspeed,

    UD​=ρ2qD​​​

    UD​=1.2232(35840.1)​​

    UD​=242.10 m/s

    When divergence occurs, determinant of matrix must be equal to zero.

    0=det​2kT​−qSCLα​​e−kT​0​−kT​2kT​−qSCLα​​e−kT​​0−kT​2kT​−qSCLα​​e​​

    0=(2kT​−qSCLα​​e)3−kT​2(2kT​−qSCLα​​e)−kT​2(2kT​−qSCLα​​e)

    0=(2kT​−qSCLα​​e)3−2kT​2(2kT​−qSCLα​​e)

    Let x=2kT​−qSCLα​​e.

    0=x3−2kT​2x

    0=x(x2−2kT​2)

    0=x(x+2​kT​)(x−2​kT​)

    x=0,−2​kT​,2​kT​

    0=2kT​−qD,1​SCLα​​e

    2​kT​=2kT​−qD,1​SCLα​​e

    qD​=SCLα​​e2kT​​,SCLα​​e(2−2​)kT​​,SCLα​​e(2+2​)kT​​

    qD​=SCLα​​e(2−2​)kT​​=0.6(5)(0.25)(2−2​)(15000)​=11715.7 N/m2

    UD​=ρ2qD​​​=1.232(11715.7)​​=138.02 m/s

    θ=qSCLα​​e+qSt​CLtα​​et​−kT​−qSCLα​​αr​e−qSt​CLtα​​αr​et​​

    #Measurement of qD​ in Practice

    Consider a symmetric airfoil such that CMac​​=0.

    θ=k−qSCLα​​eqSCLα​​αr​e​

    θ=(k/SCLα​​e)−qqαr​​

    θ=qD​−qqαr​​=(qD​/q)−1αr​​

    θ1​=αr​(qD​/q)−1​=qαr​qD​​−αr​1​

    💡

    θ1​=αr​qD​​(q1​−qD​1​)

    Let independent variable x be represented by 1/q.
    Let dependent variable     y be represented by 1/θ.
    Equation of a straight line with slope     qD​/αr​.

    #Change in Lift (Rigid vs Elastic)

    Change in lift between rigid and elastic support,

    ΔL=Lrigid​−L=qSCLα​​αr​−qSCLα​​(αr​+θ)=qSCLα​​θ

    For a rigid support, additional angle of attack θ=0 such that α=αr​.

    Percentage change in lift is given by,

    Lrigid​ΔL​=qSCLα​​αr​qSCLα​​θ​=αr​θ​

    Lrigid​ΔL​=αr​1​(qD​−qqαr​​)

    Lrigid​ΔL​=qD​−qq​

    💡

    Lrigid​ΔL​=1−q/qD​q/qD​​

    Lift increases significantly as q→qD​ until stall is reached and decreases.
    Structure will not tolerate infinite deformation and fail at a certain point.

    #Example

    Moments about elastic axis ∑M=0,

    0=Mac​+Le−Fkˉ​a

    0=Mac​+Le−(kˉaθ)a

    0=Mac​+Le−(kˉa2)θ

    where the coefficient of θ is the
    torsional stiffness of the system

    Torsional stiffness of system,

    k=kˉa2=80000(0.08)2

    k=512 Nm/rad

    Divergence dynamic pressure,

    qD​=SCLα​​ek​=(1×0.16)(6)(0.04)512​=13333.3 N/m2

    Percentage change in lift,

    Lrigid​ΔL​=1−q/qD​q/qD​​=1−5000/13333.35000/13333.3​=60%

    A wing that is allowed to deform will provide 60% higher lift than a rigid wing.

    From observation of qD​, to double divergence dynamic pressure:

    • Decrease distance e between aerodynamic center and elastic axis
    • e can be decreased by shifting the elastic axis closer to ac
    • Shifting elastic axis also changes distance a and thus k

    Let e′ be the location of the new elastic axis (pivot) from the trailing edge.

    e′=0.12−x

    Note that the elastic axis must lie behind the ac for divergence to occur.

    Location of new elastic axis (pivot),

    2qD​=SCLα​​e′k′​=SCLα​​(0.12−x)kˉx2​

    2(13333.3)=(1×0.16)(6)(0.12−x)80000x2​

    0=80000x2+25600x−3072

    x=0.092982 m

    #Rigid Wing Aileron Reversal

    Aileron reversal:

    • Downwards (+ve) deflection of aileron increases lift
    • For a flexible wing, aileron deflection may cause twisting of the wing
    • Twisting of wing generates aerodynamic forces that oppose aileron lift
    • Ailerons function in a manner opposite of its intended function which poses a danger

    Moments about the elastic axis ∑M=0,

    0=Mac​+(Lcosα)e−kθ

    kθ=Mac​+Le

    kθ=qSCMac​​c+(qSCL​)e

    For a wing with ailerons,

    CL​=CLα​​α+CLβ​​β

    CMac​​=CM0​​+CMβ​​β

    Note that CMβ​​<0 as positive deflection of
    aileron creates an anti-clockwise moment.

    Elastic deformation of the wing,

    kθ=qS(CM0​​+CMβ​​β)c+qS(CLα​​α+CLβ​​β)e

    kθ=qS(CM0​​+CMβ​​β)c+qS[CLα​​(αr​+θ)+CLβ​​β]e

    (k−qSCLα​​e)θ=qS(CM0​​+CMβ​​β)c+qS(CLα​​αr​+CLβ​​β)e

    💡

    θ=k−qSCLα​​eqS(CM0​​+CMβ​​β)c+qS(CLα​​αr​+CLβ​​β)e​

    Lift equation of the wing,

    L=qSCL​

    L=qS(CLα​​α+CLβ​​β)

    L=qSCLα​​(αr​+θ)+qSCLβ​​β

    💡

    L=qS​1−kqSCLα​​e​CLα​​(αr​+kqSCM0​​c​)+CLβ​​(1+kCLβ​​CLα​​qSCMβ​​c​)β​​

    Coefficient of β consists of two terms:

    • 1st term CLβ​​ represents aerodynamic effects, whereby ↑β results in ↑L
    • 2nd term CMβ​​ represents aeroelastic effects and is a negative term since CMβ​​<0
    • At low airspeeds (q is very small) aerodynamic effects overpower aeroelastic effects
    • As q increases, aeroelastic effects become stronger up to a point at which ∂β∂L​=0
    • At this point, any change in aileron angle has no effect on the lift of the wing
    • Aileron loses its effectiveness — aileron reversal

    Dynamic pressure at which aileron reversal occurs,

    ∂β∂L​=1−kqSCLα​​e​qSCLβ​​(1+kCLβ​​CLα​​qSCMβ​​c​)​

    0=1+kCLβ​​CLα​​qSCMβ​​c​

    💡

    qR​=−CLα​​SCMβ​​ckCLβ​​​

    A higher torsional stiffness k increases the airspeed at which aileron reversal occurs.
    Thus, actual     q<qR​ to prevent reversal. For a rigid wing, whereby k=∞, reversal
    is impossible.

    Lift equation can be rewritten with qD​ and qR​.

    💡

    L=qS[1−qD​q​CLα​​(αr​+kqSCM0​​c​)+CLβ​​(1−qR​q​)β​]

    Aileron efficiency is defined as,

    💡

    η=1−q/qD​1−q/qR​​

    When qD​qR​​=1, η=1 and it is a rigid wing. qD​qR​​≤1 as a ratio more than 1 implies that the ailerons on an elastic wing is more efficient that those on a rigid wing.

    #Example 1

    Assume angles α, β, and θ are small.

    Moments about pivot ∑M=0,

    0=Mac​+(Lcosα)e−Fk​h

    0=Mac​+Le−(kθh)h

    kh2θ=qSCMac​​c+(qSCL​)e

    kh2θ=qS(CM0​​+CMβ​​β)c+qS(CLα​​α+CLβ​​β)e

    kh2θ=qSCMβ​​βc+qS[CLα​​(αr​+θ)+CLβ​​β]e

    (kh2−qSCLα​​e)θ=qS[CLα​​αr​e+(CMβ​​c+CLβ​​e)β]

    θ=kh2−qSCLα​​eqS[CLα​​αr​e+(CMβ​​c+CLβ​​e)β]​

    Lift equation of the wing,

    L=qS[CLα​​(αr​+θ)+CLβ​​β]

    L=qS{1−(qSCLα​​e)/(kh2)CLα​​αr​+CLβ​​[1+(CLα​​qSCMβ​​c)/(kh2CLβ​​)]β​}

    Reversal dynamic pressure,

    −qR​q​=kh2CLβ​​CLα​​qSCMβ​​c​

    qR​=−CLα​​SCMβ​​ckh2CLβ​​​

    qR​=−5(0.24)(−0.25)(0.25)150000(0.06)2(0.8)​

    qR​=5760 N/m2

    Divergence dynamic pressure,

    qD​q​=kh2qSCLα​​e​

    qD​=SCLα​​ekh2​

    qD​=0.24(5)(0.05)150000(0.06)2​

    qD​=9000 N/m2

    Reversal airspeed,

    UR​=ρ2qR​​​

    UR​=1.2232(5760)​​

    UR​=97.054 m/s

    Divergence airspeed,

    UD​=ρ2qD​​​

    UD​=1.2232(9000)​​

    UD​=121.32 m/s

    Dynamic pressure for which η=0.65,

    0.65=1−q/qD​1−q/qR​​

    0.65−qD​0.65q​=1−qR​q​

    q(qR​1​−qD​0.65​)=0.35

    q=1/5760−0.65/90000.35​

    q=3452.1 N/m2

    Corresponding airspeed,

    U0.65​=ρ2q​​=1.2232(3452.1)​​=75.135 m/s

    #Example 3

    Dynamic pressure,

    q=21​(1.23)(100)2=6150 N/m2

    Moment due to elastic deformation of the wing,

    Mθ​=Lθ​e=(qSCLα​​θ)e

    Moment due to rolling of the wing,

    Mω​=Lω​e=(qSCLα​​U−v​)e=−qSCLα​​Urω​e

    As the wing generates lift, it will rotate about the pivot such that there is a downward velocity component. The resultant velocity vector of Uand rω will create a negative
    angle of attack.

    Moment due to flap deflection,

    MF​=MFac​​+LF​e

    MF​=qSCMβ​​βc+(qSCLβ​​β)e

    Flap produces a lift and moment about the ac.

    Moments about the elastic axis ∑M=0,

    0=Mθ​+Mω​+MF​−kT​θ

    0=qSCLα​​θe−qSCLα​​Urω​e+qSCMβ​​βc+qSCLβ​​βe−kT​θ

    (kT​−qSCLα​​e)θ=−qSCLα​​Urω​e+qSCMβ​​βc+qSCLβ​​βe

    Since ω is steady, angular acceleration dtdω​=0 such that L=0.

    L=Lθ​+Lω​+LF​

    0=qSCLα​​θ−qSCLα​​Urω​+qSCLβ​​β

    0=CLα​​θ−CLα​​Urω​+CLβ​​β

    θ=Urω​−CLα​​CLβ​​​β

    Substituting θ into the moments equation,

    (kT​−qSCLα​​e)(Urω​−CLα​​CLβ​​​β)=−qSCLα​​Urω​e+qSCMβ​​βc+qSCLβ​​βe

    kT​Urω​−kT​CLα​​CLβ​​​β=qSCMβ​​βc

    kT​Urω​=qSCMβ​​βc+kT​CLα​​CLβ​​​β

    kT​Urω​=CLα​​(qSCLα​​CMβ​​c+kT​CLβ​​)β​

    ω=CLα​​kT​r(qSCLα​​CMβ​​c+kT​CLβ​​)βU​

    ω=6(5000)(3.5)6150(0.2)(6)(−0.4)(0.4)+5000(1.6)​⋅18010π(100)​

    ω=1.1335 rad/s

    Substituting ω into the elastic deformation equation,

    θ=Urω​−CLα​​CLβ​​​β

    θ=1003.5(1.1335)​−61.6​⋅18010π​

    θ=−0.0068696 rad

    When reversal occurs, deflection β does not generate lift.
    Since no lift is generated, no rolling moment ω is created.

    Reversal dynamic pressure,

    0=CLα​​kT​r(qSCLα​​CMβ​​c+kT​CLβ​​)βU​

    0=qSCLα​​CMβ​​c+kT​CLβ​​

    qR​=−SCLα​​CMβ​​ckT​CLβ​​​

    qR​=−0.2(6)(−0.4)(0.4)5000(1.6)​

    qR​=41667 N/m2
